readout.purpose: Live measured values in the telemetry panels (Link latency). Always core white with glow; amber with an amber glow when a health check fails.

clock.purpose: Top-bar clock only; 17px on phones. Date line below is 10.5px HUD voice in ink 2.

wordmark.purpose: The ATLAS wordmark, centred in the top bar, uppercase, core white with glow.

core-state.purpose: The state word on the line under the core, HUD voice, signal with glow; amber without glow for Fault and Offline.

title.purpose: Systems drawer title (core white, glow); the Session log title uses the same voice at 12px.

label.purpose: Panel heads, buttons, tabs and the Systems button, HUD voice (uppercase, font-stretch 125%).

body.purpose: Message bodies, the composer input and the empty-state line, normal width, sentence case.

meta.purpose: Key-value labels, chip values, notes, module statuses, the message count and the state detail.

mono.purpose: Code blocks (13px), API routes, module build paths and key caps (11-12px), always with real casing.

shadows.name: glow
shadows.purpose: The --glow text-shadow: wordmark, clock, readout values, state word, drawer title, Atlas speaker name.

shadows.name: lit-dot
shadows.purpose: Status dots, online module dots, meter fill, streaming caret, newest latency bar (6px); amber and red versions on warn and bad chips.

shadows.name: warn-readout
shadows.purpose: Text-shadow on the Link readout when a health check fails.

shadows.name: composer-focus
shadows.purpose: Composer while focused, with a signal border.

shadows.name: drawer
shadows.purpose: Systems drawer only (opaque ground fill), over a scrim of rgba(0, 3, 6, 0.55).

shadows.name: core-light
shadows.purpose: SVG filter on the scan arc; the context arc uses drop-shadow(0 0 6px rgba(58, 216, 255, 0.8)). The Earth draws its own canvas halo.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Responses: press, hover, chevrons, message entrance, meters, context arc, value flash, boot overlay fade.

motion.name: ease-in-out
motion.purpose: Travel: the core's glide home after boot.

motion.name: ease-expo
motion.purpose: Reveals: top bar, state line and chat drawing in after boot, and the core's layers opening.

motion.name: ease-drawer
motion.purpose: The Systems drawer sliding in and out.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Buttons, the Systems button, icon buttons and tabs on :active.

motion.name: drawer
motion.purpose: Systems drawer open/close; 1ms under reduced motion.

motion.name: message-enter
motion.purpose: Each new message; boot log lines use 220ms.

motion.name: value-flash
motion.purpose: A telemetry value that just changed.

motion.name: meter-fill
motion.purpose: Context meter in the Session panel; the core's context arc uses 700ms on stroke-dasharray.

motion.name: reveal
motion.value: 620ms ease-expo, clip-path inset from the right, 90ms stagger
motion.purpose: Top bar, state line and chat draw in after boot; 300ms fade under reduced motion.

motion.name: boot-ring-open
motion.value: 1000ms ease-expo, clip-path circle(0%) to circle(75%), 90ms stagger per layer
motion.purpose: Core layers and the Earth open from the centre during boot.

motion.name: boot-glide
motion.purpose: Core returns from screen centre to its place; overlay fades 700ms.

motion.name: boot-pacing
motion.purpose: Boot log readable pacing; skipped by click, key or reduced motion.

motion.name: ring-periods
motion.value: ticks 140s cw, segments 90s ccw (coupled); scan 1.1s cw (fixed)
motion.purpose: Base rotation per ring at speed 1.

motion.name: ring-speeds
motion.value: booting 2.5, standby 1, listening 1.6, thinking 3, streaming 2 + min(chunks/s / 8, 6), error 0.4, offline 0 (instant)
motion.purpose: Playback-rate multiplier per core state; eased 6% per frame toward target.

motion.name: bloom-energy
motion.value: +0.14 per chunk (cap 1), decay x0.9 per frame
motion.purpose: Bloom scale 0.95 + 0.15*energy, opacity 0.25 + 0.6*energy.

motion.name: globe-rotation
motion.value: one turn per 70s x globe speed; globe speed = 1 + (ring target - 1) * 0.35, eased 5% per frame
motion.purpose: The Earth turns with the state but stays calm; offline stops it instantly.

motion.name: globe-voice
motion.value: +0.22 per chunk (cap 1), fades x0.18 per second; ripple sin(13d - 7.5t), 3.5% dot push; 120 voice bars at 1.07R, length R*(0.012 + 0.13*talk*n)
motion.purpose: The Earth talks while a reply streams: ripples, lit crests, jumping voice bars and a swelling halo.

motion.name: caret-blink
motion.purpose: Streaming caret; steady under reduced motion.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Rings paused, Earth stops turning and rippling (crests still brighten), bloom brightens without scaling, no boot ring-open/glide/pacing, reveal becomes a 300ms fade, message entrances and caret blink off, instant log scroll, drawer and scrim switch in 1ms.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: Same column, tighter: icon-only Systems button, dot-only Link chip, version and date hide, clock 17px, core clamp(150px, 30dvh, 240px), chat box edge to edge.

components.css: .ds-ground { background: var(--ground, #02060a); padding: 20px; color: var(--ink, #d8f6ff); font-family: var(--font, "Saira", system-ui, "Segoe UI", sans-serif); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-log { width: 420px; max-width: 100%; } .ds-msg { margin: 0 0 20px; } .ds-msg-head { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 10px; margin-bottom: 6px; } .ds-msg-who { font-size: 10.5px; font-weight: 700; color: var(--ink-2, #8fc7da); font-stretch: 125%; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.14em; } .ds-msg--atlas .ds-msg-who { color: var(--signal, #3ad8ff); text-shadow: var(--glow, 0 0 14px rgba(58, 216, 255, 0.55)); } .ds-msg--error .ds-msg-who { color: var(--amber, #ffb84d); } .ds-msg-meta { font-size: 12px; color: var(--ink-3, #6fa3b6); } .ds-msg-time { margin-left: auto; font-size: 12px; color: var(--ink-3, #6fa3b6); } .ds-msg-body { font-size: var(--fs-body, 15px); line-height: 1.55; color: var(--ink, #d8f6ff); overflow-wrap: anywhere; } .ds-msg--user .ds-msg-body { padding: 10px 14px; border: 1px solid var(--line, rgba(90, 205, 255, 0.2)); background: var(--raised, rgba(57, 213, 255, 0.07)); white-space: pre-wrap; } .ds-msg--error .ds-msg-body { padding: 10px 14px; border: 1px solid rgba(255, 184, 77, 0.4); background: var(--amber-soft, rgba(255, 184, 77, 0.14)); color: #ffd9a1; } .ds-msg-raw { margin: 6px 0 0; font-family: var(--mono, ui-monospace, Consolas, monospace); font-size: 12px; color: #d9a866; } .ds-caret { display: inline-block; width: 0.55em; height: 1.05em; margin-left: 2px; vertical-align: -0.15em; background: var(--signal, #3ad8ff); box-shadow: 0 0 8px var(--signal, #3ad8ff); animation: ds-caret 1s steps(1) infinite; } @keyframes ds-caret { 50% { opacity: 0; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-caret { animation: none; } }

narrative.overview:
Atlas is a heads-up display projected onto a blue-black table: a faint 32px grid, light falling off from the Earth near the top of the screen, and every structure drawn in translucent cyan light rather than grey. The core sits at the top of one centred column. It is a dot-matrix holographic Earth inside rotating rings, and it is the model made visible. While the model thinks, a scan arc sweeps the rings. While a reply streams, every chunk makes the Earth talk: ripples run across its land dots and voice bars jump around its rim. The rings spin faster with the measured stream rate, and everything stops dead when the backend is gone. The spectacle is real telemetry in costume.

The screen is deliberately quiet. The owner asked for less clutter, so the main view holds only a three-part top bar, the core with a one-line state readout, and the chat box beneath it, which takes the rest of the height. Telemetry and the module list sit one click away in a Systems drawer on the left. Reading stays calm: normal-width 15px type in a darker frame no wider than 780px. The owner's binding reference is the cinematic holographic HUD: cyan on black, a circular core, a boot sequence. Atlas builds its own HUD from that grammar and copies no film props or studio marks.

The world rejects the category default for chat, a conversation sidebar beside a centred transcript. Chat is the job, and it sits directly under the instrument that shows the model working.
keyCharacteristics: One hue family (cyan, roughly 209–239° in OKLCH) on a near-black ground; amber and red are status voices only.
Structure in light: 1px translucent cyan frames, with brighter 2px corner brackets on instrument regions.
One variable typeface, Saira, in two widths: expanded tracked capitals for labels, normal width for reading.
Glow is emission. It belongs to the core and the Earth, the identity marks, the clock, live values and lit status.
One centred column: core, state line, chat. Everything else lives in the Systems drawer.
The rings' speed and the Earth's voice are coupled to app state and to the measured stream.
Every number is measured, labelled as an estimate, or an em dash that names the route it is waiting for.

rules.name: The Structure-in-Light Rule
rules.body: Frames, dividers, meter tracks and scrollbars are cyan at reduced alpha (line at 20%, line-strong at 42%). There are no grey borders anywhere in the world.

rules.name: The Status Voice Rule
rules.body: Cyan means live and answering. Amber means it exists but isn't working (stub, waiting, warning, fault, offline core). Red is only a dead Link chip. Amber and red are never decorative.

rules.name: The Contrast Floor Rule
rules.body: Every ink token clears 4.5:1 on the ground and on panel glass. Ink 3, the faintest, measures about 7.3:1 on the ground and 5.4:1 on the raised tint. New text colours meet the same floor.

rules.name: The Two Widths Rule
rules.body: Expanded tracked capitals are for labels only: panel heads, chip labels, buttons, tabs, the Systems button, speaker names, the state word, the wordmark, the drawer title and the date line. Anything a person reads as a sentence is normal width and sentence case.

rules.name: The Real Spelling Rule
rules.body: API routes and file paths keep their real, case-sensitive spelling in mono, even next to an uppercase HUD label (panel subheads, boot log lines, module build paths).

rules.name: The One Column Rule
rules.body: The main screen is the core, its state line and the chat, centred, and nothing else. Telemetry, module status and controls that are not about the conversation go in the Systems drawer, not the column, the corners or the top bar.

rules.name: The Log Keeps Its Height Rule
rules.body: The core is sized from viewport height so the session log and composer always fill what remains. Nothing pushes them below the fold.

rules.name: The Emission-Not-Elevation Rule
rules.body: Cyan glow marks light that is live: the core and the Earth, the identity marks, the clock, measured values, the state word and lit status. Body text, panel heads and static frames never glow.

rules.name: The Floating-Goes-Opaque Rule
rules.body: Only the Systems drawer carries a dark drop shadow, and it has an opaque ground fill over a dimming scrim, so its text never sits over the turning rings.

rules.name: The Bracket Placement Rule
rules.body: Corner brackets mark instrument regions: a diagonal pair on telemetry panels and on the chat box, arcs on the core. Chips, buttons, tabs, messages and module rows carry plain 1px frames or rules.

rules.name: The Honest Readout Rule
rules.body: A value is measured; or labelled as an estimate ("≈", "estimated", "(browser)"); or an em dash with a note naming the route and phase that will supply it. There are no placeholder numbers and no simulated graphs.

rules.name: The Lit-Only-When-Built Rule
rules.body: A module turns cyan only when its route answers. There is no "coming soon" glow.

rules.name: The Coupled Rotation Rule
rules.body: The rings' speed and the Earth's voice are the app's state plus the measured stream: one chunk, one pulse. Never a decorative timer. A dead link stops the rings and the Earth dead.

rules.name: The Still-But-Readable Rule
rules.body: With reduced motion nothing rotates or travels across the screen, but every state still reads through colour and brightness.

dos: **Do** draw every frame and divider in cyan light: line (rgba(90, 205, 255, 0.2)) by default, line-strong (rgba(110, 220, 255, 0.42)) for controls and the drawer's edge.
**Do** set labels in Saira at 125% width, uppercase, 0.14em tracking, and set everything people read at normal width in sentence case.
**Do** keep API routes and file paths in mono with their real casing.
**Do** show a missing value as an em dash with a note naming the route and phase that will supply it, and label estimates as estimates.
**Do** drive any new core or Earth behaviour from measured data through the state speed table and the per-chunk pulse, never from a decorative timer.
**Do** use amber for anything that exists but isn't working yet, and keep red for a dead link.
**Do** put new instruments, telemetry and module controls in the Systems drawer, as a panel or a tab, and keep the main column to the core, the state line and the chat.
**Do** give floating layers an opaque fill and the dark drop shadow, and keep in-flow panels translucent and shadowless.
**Do** keep hover styles inside `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)` and give buttons, the Systems button and tabs a 0.97 press scale.
donts: **Don't** add grey borders, grey text or an untinted neutral; every neutral in the world leans toward the cyan hue.
**Don't** invent numbers, sparklines or simulated telemetry to fill a panel.
**Don't** light a module cyan before its route answers.
**Don't** add glow to body text, panel heads or static frames.
**Don't** introduce rounded cards, pill buttons or large radii; the world is square, with a 2px concession on controls.
**Don't** put status chips, module markers, suggested prompts or side panels back on the main screen; the owner chose a decluttered view, and the drawer is where they go.
**Don't** let the core or anything above the chat push the session log and composer below the fold.
**Don't** add a second display or body typeface; Saira's width axis carries the hierarchy, and mono is for code, routes and key caps only.
**Don't** rebuild the chat as a conversation sidebar beside a centred transcript.
